General situation: Over the past 30 days, Brazilian corn FOB Santos prices have remained elevated at approximately 112.7 USD/ton as of March 12, 2026, while Brazilian soybeans and wheat prices both stood near 662.9 USD/ton by mid-March. US corn and soybeans spot prices were stable around 394.5 USD/ton as of early February 2026, with no recent updates to indicate significant shifts. Argentina's barley and rice prices are recorded at 212 USD/ton for late 2025, showing no recent market movement. What changed vs previous comparable period: No new temporal metrics or records are available for direct month-on-month comparison, indicating a stable price environment without notable volatility or trend shifts in non-Ukraine markets. Actionable implications for trading/brokerage: Traders should monitor Brazilian corn and soybean prices for potential export opportunities given their firm levels, while US market prices appear steady but dated, suggesting limited immediate arbitrage. Broker desk activity shows active rapeseed trades at 500 EUR/ton for August delivery and corn CIF offers at 241 EUR/ton for April, signaling ongoing demand and supply negotiations in European markets. 

Key facts:
- Brazilian corn FOB Santos at 112.7 USD/ton (March 12, 2026)
- Brazilian soybeans and wheat at 662.9 USD/ton (March 14, 2026)
- US corn and soybeans spot prices at 394.5 USD/ton (February 4, 2026)
- Argentine barley and rice at 212 USD/ton (December 31, 2025)
- Rapeseed traded at 500 EUR/ton for August 2026 delivery (March 30, 2026)
- Corn CIF offers at 241 EUR/ton for April shipment (March 25, 2026)
